newsitem.title: SPAIN: Floods in southern Spain hit roads, homes.
newsitem.headline: Floods in southern Spain hit roads, homes.

text.p: Heavy rains in southern Spain caused flooding on Sunday that cut off roads and forced several hundred people from their homes, regional officials said.
Rivers spilled over their banks, roads were awash and fields flooded as the rains, which started about a week ago, continued to pelt the region of Andalusia.
Meterologists said the wet weather would continue on Monday with some light rains and high winds.
The Atlantic coastal towns of Chiclano and Puerto de Santa Maria were hardest hit.
In Chiclano, the Iro river overflowed and flooded the low lying parts of town where rescuers had to use rubber rafts to evacuate some 200 people from their homes.
One man had to be lifted from the roof of his house by helicopter.
Another 300 people also abandoned their homes throughout the region on Saturday and Sunday, officials said.
No one has died as a result of the floods, but one young man disappeared after the car he was in slid into the swollen Guadalete river in Jerez de la Frontera.

Two other people who had been in the car when it went into the river were rescued. They had been in a high speed car chase fleeing the Spanish Civil Guard, which suspected them of looting evacuated homes.

Some 25 secondary roads in the provinces of Cadiz, Seville, Cordoba, Granada, Huelva and Malaga were closed because of flooding and the region's traffic management centre urged caution because high winds were making driving danagerous.
The state railway Renfe suspended service in Jerez de la Frontera and Puerto de Santa Maria and between Seville and Huelva due to flooding.
The rains also damaged olive, strawberry and winter grain crops, although the region's agriculture councillor said it was difficult to get to the fields to see how badly they were hit.
